source_text: Tantum ergo valet ista distinctio, ut si nescientes, quod a possibili incipit, in necessarium concludamus, omnia crimina ad Deum recurrant. Quod Manichaeus videns, tenebras peccati excogitavit auctores; non enim valuit inter possibile necessariumque distinguere. Omne ergo quod naturaliter habet homo, a necessarii parte sortitus est; quia non potuit aliter esse quam factus est.
pass_a_gloss: This distinction therefore avails so much, that if not knowing, what begins from the possible, we close into the necessary, all charges run back to God. Which Manichaeus seeing, thought out darknesses as authors of sin; for he was not able to distinguish between the possible and the necessary. Everything therefore which the human has naturally, he received from the side of the necessary; because he could not otherwise be than he was made.

lemmas.lexica: LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: This distinction has such force that, if through ignorance we conclude in necessity what begins from possibility, every crime returns to God. Mani saw this and invented darkness as sin’s author, since he could not distinguish possibility from necessity. Everything a human being possesses naturally, therefore, he has received on the side of necessity, because he could not be otherwise than he was made.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
